entities.summary:
Alcibiades was an Athenian statesman and general, born into the influential Alcmaeonidae family around 450 BCE.

As a member of the aristocratic Alcmaeonidae, Alcibiades was groomed for leadership from an early age, receiving tutelage from some of the most prominent Athenian orators and politicians of his time.

Alcibiades played a pivotal role in the second half of the Peloponnesian War, serving as a strategic advisor, military commander, and politician, and was known for his cunning and eloquence.

However, Alcibiades' ascent to power was marked by controversy, as he was accused of collaborating with the enemy and engaging in treacherous behavior, including the infamous Sphakteria affair.

Despite his fall from prominence, Alcibiades' legacy continued to shape Athenian politics and society, with many of his policies and ideas influencing the development of Western democracy.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Alcibiades' name has become synonymous with cunning and ambition, and his life has been immortalized in literature and art for centuries.
